Mozilla Ion Privacy Notice

October 30, 2020

Ion is an experimental initiative led by Mozilla to better understand how our users use and navigate the internet. Ion is available to Firefox desktop users in the United States who are 19 or older. In this Privacy Notice, we detail what data the Ion program collects and discloses, and why.

When you join Mozilla Ion, we’ll collect basic technical and interaction data as long as you’re participating in the program. Once you’ve enrolled, you’ll also have the opportunity to join available studies—each study will have a specific research purpose and a unique privacy notice for you to review before you join it.

Read each study’s privacy notice for information about how data is collected and handled in that particular study. We also adhere to the Mozilla Privacy Policy for how we receive, handle, and share information.

What Information We Collect:

Technical data: We collect information about your device’s operating system and your version of Firefox. When Firefox sends data to us, your IP address is also temporarily collected as part of our server logs.

Interaction data: We collect data about your interactions with Firefox, like number and type of installed Firefox Add-ons and how much time you use Firefox.

Location data: We will use your IP address to approximate your country, state, and city location.

To see a full list of the data we collect, click here.

How We Use Your Information:

We use the information we collect for for research and development, including:

  • To ensure our data sets are representative of the many users of Firefox
  • To improve our existing products and services
  • To create and develop new products

Who We May Disclose Information To:

Google Cloud Platform (GCP): We use GCP as our cloud-storage service. Mozilla has contracted with GCP requiring them to store the data only, and to do so in ways that are approved by us.

Third-party researchers: As part of being part of the Ion program, we will offer you the ability to join studies. If necessary for the study, we may ask you to share all or some of the data collected under this Privacy Notice with the third party researcher(s) administering the study. Read each study’s unique privacy notice for information about how data is collected and handled in that particular study.

General public: To advance our mission of being open, we may release data sets to the general public. When we do so, we will aggregate the data and remove identifying information, so the data won’t reveal the behaviors or characteristics of individual users.

Data Management:

You can learn more about managing your Pioneer and individual study data here.

If you have any other questions regarding our privacy practices, please contact us at compliance@mozilla.com.
